title: Disabled buttons you can still see
question: A button that can't be pressed yet ("Add the note" before you've written anything) is nearly invisible today: its label is 1.7:1 in the admin panel and its shape doesn't show at all. Each option below keeps the label readable (5.5:1 or more) in light and dark. Which look should a disabled button have everywhere, in the app and the admin panel?

options.label: Outline
options.lineage: the empty version of the button
options.thesis: A disabled button loses its fill and keeps a clear outline and grey label: obviously a button, obviously not ready.
options.viewport: Light and dark: the note box with "Add the note" disabled, a row of Save, Cancel and Delete enabled then disabled, and a disabled Publish on the masthead.
options.risk: The strongest difference from enabled, but an outlined button can read as a secondary action rather than an unavailable one.

options.label: Quiet grey fill
options.lineage: system buttons on iOS and macOS
options.thesis: Every disabled button becomes the same soft grey pill with a faint edge and a grey label, whatever colour it was.
options.viewport: Light and dark: the note box with "Add the note" disabled, a row of Save, Cancel and Delete enabled then disabled, and a disabled Publish on the masthead.
options.risk: The quietest option: the shape shows, but less boldly than an outline, and it no longer hints which button will be the main one.

options.label: Faded colour
options.lineage: the button's own colour, washed out
options.thesis: A disabled button keeps a pale version of its own colour, so you can see which one will be the main action once it's ready.
options.viewport: Light and dark: the note box with "Add the note" disabled, a row of Save, Cancel and Delete enabled then disabled, and a disabled Publish on the masthead.
options.risk: In dark mode the faded teal is close enough to the real one that someone may try to press it.
